diagnostics.notes: Both claims verified against their sources. A: meta-analysis of four CVOTs, GLP-1 RA vs placebo, explicit statement of no significant effect on fatal and non-fatal myocardial infarction (sentence 9). B: network meta-analysis, GLP-1 RA vs standard treatments, reported benefit in reducing non-fatal myocardial infarction (sentence 10). Same exposure class, similar outcome, comparable between-group contrasts. A's authors explicitly report no effect on MI while B reports a reduction, so the not_replicated branch applies regardless of sign agreement.

source_evidence.quote: No significant effect of GLP-1 receptor agonists was identified on fatal and non-fatal myocardial infarction, fatal and non-fatal stroke, hospital admission for unstable angina, or hospital admission for heart failure.

The study confirmed the benefits of SGLT-2 inhibitors and GLP-1 receptor agonists in reducing cardiovascular death, non-fatal myocardial infarction, admission to hospital for heart failure, and end stage kidney disease.

verdict.label: not_replicated
verdict.rationale: Both findings concern GLP-1 receptor agonists and myocardial infarction in adults with type 2 diabetes, with between-group contrasts (vs placebo in A; vs standard treatments in B). Abstract A explicitly concludes no significant effect of GLP-1 receptor agonists on fatal and non-fatal myocardial infarction, whereas abstract B reports a benefit of GLP-1 receptor agonists in reducing non-fatal myocardial infarction. An explicit no-effect conclusion against a reported effect takes the not_replicated branch; the differing comparator (placebo vs standard treatments) is noted but the decision is driven by the explicit no-effect statement.
